title: Insight 1: Nov 8 ride breached easy ceiling by ~13 bpm
description: Your November 8 ride averaged 152 bpm, which sits in Zone 2 (139–159) rather than Zone 1 (<139). If that was meant as an easy spin, keep future recovery rides under 139 bpm to truly build aerobic base without extra fatigue.

title: Insight 2: Nov 12 long ride carried 506 m elevation in 50 km
description: The November 12 ride packed 506 m of climbing over 50 km (10 m/km), noticeably hillier than your flatter 62 km ride on Nov 8 (265 m, 4 m/km). That vertical load adds strength but also fatigue — consider a flatter route next long ride if legs feel heavy.

title: Insight 3: Seven rides in 14 days with back-to-back Nov 18–19
description: You rode seven times between Nov 8–21, including consecutive days on Nov 18 (51 km) and Nov 19 (12.5 km). That density can sneak up on recovery; try inserting a rest day or very easy spin after two hard days in a row.

title: Insight 4: Cycling VO2max rose from 49 to 51 in three weeks
description: Garmin cycling VO2max climbed from 49 (Oct 30) to 51 (Nov 21), and your estimated FTP of 213 W supports the gain. Consistent riding around 150–185 W normalized power is paying off — keep the rhythm.

title: Insight 5: HR and power zones align around LTHR 175 and FTP 213 W
description: Your lactate threshold HR of 175 bpm and FTP of 213 W create consistent zones: Zone 2 power (117–160 W) matches Zone 2 HR (139–159 bpm) on most rides. No major mismatch detected; zones are usable as-is.

title: Insight 6: Recent rides show ~90% moderate (Zone 2), ~10% easy, 0% hard
description: All seven recent rides averaged in Zone 2 (135–152 bpm) except one short Zone 1 spin (Nov 19, 104 bpm). For polarized benefits, aim for 80% easy (Zone 1) and 20% hard (Zone 4+) — add one weekly interval session and make two rides truly easy.

title: Insight 7: Readiness dipped to 72 on Nov 19 but rebounded to 85 by Nov 21
description: After a short sleep night (5h30m) and higher stress (36) on Nov 19, readiness dropped to 72, but HRV rose to 78 and readiness hit 85 two days later. The trend is positive — listen to the dips, but no red flags.

title: Insight 8: No strength training data in the last 30 days
description: Cycling data shows no dedicated strength work. Adding 1–2 weekly sessions of maximal/reactive exercises (e.g., squats, plyometrics) can improve power durability and injury resilience without riding more.

title: Insight 9: Try 4×5 min at 225–235 W (105–110% FTP) to boost VO2max
description: Your FTP is ~213 W; VO2max intervals at 225–235 W for 4–5 minutes with equal recovery, once a week, can lift your 51 VO2max further. Start with 3×4 min if new to hard intervals.

title: Insight 10: Update FTP with a fresh 20-min test — current 213 W is estimated
description: The 213 W FTP comes from 95% of your best 20-min power (224 W on Nov 12), not a dedicated test. A proper 20-min all-out effort (or a ramp test) will give a more accurate anchor for power zones.
